items.headline: Singapore disputes US findings as Washington proposes a 20% tariff on its exports
items.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said it was 'very disappointed' and disagreed with the US Trade Representative's findings after Washington proposed a tariff of up to 20% on Singapore's exports; the rate could fall to 10% under a reciprocal-trade agreement.

items.headline: Singapore man jailed for making his young son ride an HDB lift naked as punishment
items.summary: A 40-year-old man was sentenced to six months' jail after making his son strip and ride the lift to the ground floor of their HDB block as punishment; he pleaded guilty, with two other charges taken into consideration.

items.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses without a deal, the first failure since 2009
items.summary: The COP31 talks in Antalya, Turkey ended with no agreement - the first time a UN climate summit has failed to adopt a deal since Copenhagen in 2009 - after the EU and other nations rejected a text that omitted any mention of moving away from fossil fuels; attention now turns to COP32.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill a senior Gaza education official and seven others despite the ceasefire
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that Israeli attacks across Gaza killed at least eight Palestinians, including a senior education ministry undersecretary and his wife; health officials say more than 1,600 people have been killed since the October ceasefire took effect.

items.headline: AI data centres are getting harder to build as Nvidia holds back financing
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that 'neocloud' data-centre operators are squeezed by construction delays and pricier debt, as Nvidia signals it will not backstop a site until it is nearly ready to run - a sign of strain in the AI build-out.

items.headline: Cybersecurity startup Corma reaches a $1 billion valuation within months
items.summary: AI cybersecurity startup Corma raised a $125 million Series A led by NEA, reaching a $1 billion valuation about three months after launching, TechCrunch reported.

items.headline: Bret Taylor's AI-agent startup Sierra is in talks to raise at a $30 billion valuation
items.summary: Sierra, the enterprise AI-agent company led by Bret Taylor, is in early talks to raise about $1.5 billion at a roughly $30 billion valuation - nearly double its May mark - The Information reported.

items.headline: India win the toss and bowl first in the series-deciding second Test at Christchurch
items.summary: Captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl first against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in the second Test, the decider after a drawn opener in Wellington; Gurnoor Brar was handed his Test debut and Mohammed Siraj was left out.

items.headline: Italy reach the Davis Cup semi-finals, edging debutants South Korea in Bologna
items.summary: Holders Italy beat Davis Cup Final 8 debutants South Korea 2-1 in Bologna, with Matteo Berrettini and Andrea Vavassori winning the decisive doubles to carry the defending champions into the semi-finals.

items.headline: Great Britain beat Germany to reach the Davis Cup semi-finals in Bologna
items.summary: Great Britain defeated Germany in their Davis Cup Final 8 quarter-final to reach the last four in Bologna, setting up a semi-final against Spain.

items.headline: Formula 1 reaches Lusail for the penultimate round, the Qatar Grand Prix
items.summary: Formula 1's title-settled season reaches its penultimate round at the Qatar Grand Prix in Lusail, running from Friday to Sunday, with the fights for the runner-up places in both the drivers' and constructors' standings still live.

items.headline: Mathematicians scrutinise rival AI and human claims of a Riemann hypothesis proof
items.summary: Two competing claimed proofs of the Riemann hypothesis - one from Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge working with Claude and formalised in the Lean proof assistant, the other credited to Stanford's Alessandro Masullo - are being pored over by mathematicians, with figures such as Terence Tao and James Maynard calling the work potentially historic but, so far, unverified.

items.headline: Blood 'fossil record' traces leukaemia back decades before diagnosis
items.summary: A Nature study by Cambridge and UCL researchers, using stored annual blood samples, found that the first driver mutations behind acute myeloid leukaemia can appear before age 20 - sometimes more than 50 years before diagnosis - suggesting that slowing a high-risk cell clone early could head off the cancer.

fun_fact.headline: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way
fun_fact.body: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way. A 2015 study in the journal Nature estimated the planet holds about 3 trillion trees, while our galaxy is thought to contain only 100 billion to 400 billion stars. The tree figure was itself a surprise - more than seven times the previous estimate - and came from pairing satellite imagery with ground counts.
fun_fact.source: Nature (Crowther et al., 2015, ~3.04 trillion trees) and its accompanying commentary; Yale; Scientific American

puzzle.title: Three Hats in a Line
puzzle.body: Three logicians - Amir, Bina and Carl - stand single-file, each seeing only those in front. From 3 black hats and 2 white hats, one is placed on each head; the other two are hidden. Amir (back, sees Bina and Carl): 'I can't tell my hat colour.' Bina (middle, sees Carl): 'I can't tell either.' Carl (front, sees no one): 'Then I know mine.' What colour is Carl's hat?
puzzle.approach: Work through what each person's silence rules out for those in front.
puzzle.answer: Black. If Amir saw two white hats he would know his own is black (only 2 white hats), so Bina and Carl are not both white. Bina, seeing only Carl, would know her own is black if Carl were white; since she can't tell, Carl is not white. Carl therefore deduces his hat is black.

word_puzzle.title: Raining Cats and Dogs
word_puzzle.body: Turn CATS into DOGS, changing exactly one letter at each step, with every rung a valid English word. It can be done in three steps.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time, keeping every rung a real word.
word_puzzle.answer: CATS -> COTS -> COGS -> DOGS. CATS to COTS (a->o, a cot is a small bed); COTS to COGS (t->g, gear teeth); COGS to DOGS (c->d). Three one-letter changes, each a real word.
